# The Housing Helpline

> Claims management company helping tenants in England with housing disrepair and tenancy deposit claims. The Housing Helpline is part of Claim 3000 Ltd (Manchester, FCA firm reference 833604, regulated for housing disrepair claims). It checks whether tenants could claim and introduces them to independent regulated solicitors. You do not need to use a claims management company: you can complain to your landlord and then the Housing Ombudsman, or use your deposit scheme's dispute service, for free.

Phone 0161 541 2053 (Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm). Email contact@claim3000.co.uk.

## Questions and answers

### Is the check really free?

Yes. Checking costs nothing and does not commit you to a claim.

### Who will I deal with?

Us first: we check whether you could claim and talk your options through with you. If you go ahead, we introduce you to an independent regulated solicitor, who handles your claim.

### How long does it take?

About 60 seconds online. We aim to reply within 2 working days.

### Do I need evidence to start?

No. Photos, messages to your landlord and receipts all help, and we will tell you what else would help.

### What does it cost if I go ahead?

The solicitor explains their fees in writing before you agree to anything, so you know where you stand first.

### Will my landlord evict me for claiming?

Since 1 May 2026, a landlord can no longer evict you with a "no fault" section 21 notice. They need a legal reason, called a ground for possession.

### Is there a time limit?

For disrepair, yes: up to 6 years from when your landlord should have done the work, or 3 years if you are claiming for an injury to your health. The sooner you check, the better.

### What is housing disrepair?

Housing disrepair is when your landlord has not kept your rented home in repair or fit to live in. Under the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985, landlords must keep the structure and exterior in repair, along with the water, gas, electricity, heating and sanitation, and since 2019 the home must be fit to live in for the whole tenancy.

### Can I claim compensation for housing disrepair?

You may be able to claim if you rent from the council or a housing association in England, you told your landlord about the problem, and it still has not been put right. A claim can lead to compensation and to a court ordering the repairs.

### How much compensation could I get for housing disrepair?

There is no fixed amount. It depends on how bad the problem was, how long it lasted and how it affected you, including damaged belongings, extra costs and your health.

### What is Awaab's Law?

Awaab's Law sets repair deadlines for council and housing association landlords in England, in force since 27 October 2025. They must make an emergency hazard safe within 24 hours, investigate significant damp and mould within 10 working days, and do the safety work within 5 working days after that.

### How long do I have to make a housing disrepair claim?

Up to 6 years from when your landlord should have done the work, or 3 years if you are claiming for an injury to your health.

### What does it mean for a tenancy deposit to be protected?

It means your landlord or letting agent has put your deposit in a government-approved tenancy deposit scheme within 30 days of receiving it. The three schemes in England are the Deposit Protection Service, MyDeposits and the Tenancy Deposit Scheme.

### What can I do if my landlord did not protect my deposit?

You can claim. A court can order your landlord to return or protect the deposit and to pay you up to 3 times the deposit.

### What must my landlord tell me about my deposit?

Within 30 days of getting your deposit, your landlord must tell you in writing which scheme holds it, how much you paid, how it is protected, why they might keep some of it and how to get it back.

### How long does a landlord have to return my deposit?

Your landlord must return your deposit within 10 days of you both agreeing how much you get back.

### Do deposit rules still apply after 1 May 2026?

Yes. Most assured shorthold tenancies became assured periodic tenancies on 1 May 2026, and the deposit protection rules still apply.

### Can I claim if I have moved out?

For a deposit, yes: if it was not protected, you can still claim after your tenancy has ended. For disrepair, we help while you are living in the home.

### How much could I get for my deposit?

If your deposit was not protected, a court can order your landlord to pay you up to 3 times the deposit, as well as returning or protecting it.

### What happens after I start?

We talk your options through with you and, if you go ahead, introduce you to an independent regulated solicitor. For disrepair, your solicitor writes to your landlord with a letter of claim, the landlord should normally reply within 20 working days, and an independent inspection then records what needs doing.

### Do I keep paying rent?

Yes. Keep paying your rent while you wait for repairs, and let your landlord in to inspect or do the work.

### I live in Wales, Scotland or Northern Ireland

Different laws apply there, so this site does not cover you. Call us and we will point you the right way.

### Are you solicitors?

No. The Housing Helpline is a claims management company, regulated by the FCA for housing disrepair claims. We introduce you to an independent regulated solicitor, who handles your claim.

### Who are The Housing Helpline?

The Housing Helpline is part of Claim 3000 Ltd, a Manchester claims management company incorporated in 2015. It helps tenants in England check whether they could make a housing disrepair or tenancy deposit claim and introduces them to independent regulated solicitors.

### Is The Housing Helpline regulated?

Yes, for housing disrepair claims. Claim 3000 Ltd is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority for claims management activity, firm reference 833604.
